events.subtitle: Guitar Icons: St. Vincent

venue.name: Grace Rainey Rogers Auditorium at The Metropolitan Museum of Art

events.category: Art rock / guitar history / museum-specific collaboration
events.factual_description: The Metropolitan Museum of Art presents Guitar Icons: St. Vincent on Saturday, February 20, 2027 at 7:00 PM in the Grace Rainey Rogers Auditorium. The Met says the one-night performance will feature a historical instrument from its collection as part of the Guitar Icons series connected to the museum's forthcoming gallery celebrating the American guitar. The Met's 2026-27 season announcement also states that St. Vincent will be joined by keyboardist Rachel Eckroth for the performance. Tickets are listed at $35-$155 in the season announcement, while the current Met Live Arts hub lists tickets starting at $35. The exact historical instrument and detailed repertoire are not identified in the accessible primary materials, so neither is inferred here.

en.why_it_matters: This is not just St. Vincent in a smaller New York room. The Met is putting one of contemporary art-rock's most distinctive guitar voices inside a series about the cultural history of the American guitar, handing the performance a historical instrument from its own collection and pairing Clark with Rachel Eckroth on keyboards. The instrument is part of the idea of the night: a modern player known for reshaping electric-guitar language is being asked to put that language in direct contact with the museum's material history.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is already in play that weekend, actively build Saturday around The Met; this museum-and-instrument framing will not behave like a normal tour stop. From the DMV, I would pair it with another strong New York reason rather than make a dedicated up-and-back trip solely for this engagement.

es.why_it_matters: No es simplemente St. Vincent en una sala más pequeña de Nueva York. The Met coloca una de las voces más reconocibles de la guitarra en el art rock contemporáneo dentro de una serie sobre la historia cultural de la guitarra estadounidense, incorpora un instrumento histórico de su propia colección y suma a Rachel Eckroth en teclados. El instrumento forma parte de la idea de la noche: una guitarrista que lleva años deformando y expandiendo el lenguaje eléctrico entra en contacto directo con la historia material que conserva el museo.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya entra en el plan ese fin de semana, sí armaría el sábado alrededor de The Met; este cruce entre museo e instrumento no se comporta como una parada normal de gira. Desde el DMV, lo combinaría con otra razón fuerte para subir en vez de hacer un viaje dedicado de ida y vuelta únicamente por esta función.
